column1: Phase budget - where the cycle time goes

All 93 logged cycles are one continuous run (2026-09-04 20:13-20:29, seq 1-93). 'Clean' below excludes seq 93 (see Summary). There is no branch-B / feed-pass concept on this cell - PlateSorter always places to accept or reject.

column7: PartPick.pgx: the APERA-planned APPROACH move, through its waitEndMove(). Also absorbs any motion still queued from the end of the PREVIOUS cycle's PartPlace (retreat + return-to-Start) - see the CycleDataLogging_2026-09-04 bundle README for why that can't be split out without adding a new waitEndMove().
PartPick.pgx: air-blast on + the LINEAR_APPROACH move down onto the part, through its waitEndMove(). Very consistent (0.33-0.55s) - almost pure dwell/short motion, little variance.

PartPick.pgx: the blocking call tTool("ON") itself - the Schunk EGM gripper's magnetize delay. Constant 0.50s every cycle (wait(Mag==true) + delay(0.5) inside tTool.pgx) - this is a fixed dwell, not motion.
PartPlace.pgx: entry through the waitEndMove() that lands the part at whichever destination (accept/reject/feed conveyor) that pick used.
PartPlace.pgx: the blocking call tTool("OFF") itself - the gripper's de-magnetize delay. Constant 1.00s every cycle - fixed dwell.

tkCycle.pgx: taskCreate "PartFinder" through wait(taskStatus==1) - the async task's launch/dispatch, not its result. Reads 0.00s every cycle - launching a task is near-instant; the real vision cost shows up as Finder wait below.

tkCycle.pgx: wait(bRunning["PartFinder"]==false) after PartPlace() returns - the extra time (if any) spent waiting for the async PartFinder vision task to finish once the pick+place motion was already done. This is the real, visible cost of vision on this cell (avg ~0.8s) - it just shows up as a wait rather than inside a motion segment.
cycle_s directly - clock() at the top and bottom of tkCycle's if-branch.

Essentially zero - the 7 segments plus the small gaps between them (queueing, not waited on) already cover the whole cycle, unlike 1RT53's coarser split. This is a much tighter accounting than 1RT53's cell, likely because PlateSorter's retreat-carry-over is small relative to its cycle time.
